answer: The original source is Freddie Mac, from its Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS). FRED carries it as the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States (series MORTGAGE30US), in percent, not seasonally adjusted. It is published weekly, normally on Thursdays. The series goes back to April 1971.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC. FRED's copy (series SP500, daily closing index level) only covers a rolling window of about the most recent 10 years, because of licensing limits, so as of October 2026 it would start around October 2016. It is not the full history of the index, and it is a price index that excludes dividends.

The source is S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC, which publishes it as the S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller U.S. National Home Price Index (FRED series CSUSHPINSA, not seasonally adjusted, and CSUSHPISA, seasonally adjusted). It is a monthly index with January 2000 = 100. Note: the index branding may have changed recently (CoreLogic was rebranded as Cotality in 2025), so the current title on FRED may read differently; I am not certain of the exact present wording.

It comes from the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers. FRED carries it as University of Michigan: Consumer Sentiment (series UMCSENT), a monthly index with 1966:Q1 = 100, not seasonally adjusted. At the source's request, FRED shows it with a one-month delay.

The source is the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA). FRED carries it as Crude Oil Prices: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) - Cushing, Oklahoma (series DCOILWTICO), daily, in dollars per barrel, not seasonally adjusted, starting in January 1986.

The source is the U.S. Employment and Training Administration (ETA), part of the U.S. Department of Labor, from its weekly Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims report. Yes, the headline series (Initial Claims, FRED series ICSA) is seasonally adjusted; it is weekly, in number of claims, for weeks ending Saturday. A not seasonally adjusted version (ICNSA) is also available.

FRED's headline real GDP series (GDPC1) is reported in billions of chained 2017 dollars, at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, quarterly. The source is the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). The reference year was 2017 as of my knowledge; BEA changes it at comprehensive revisions, so it is worth checking that it has not been updated since.

FRED's headline CPI-U series (CPIAUCSL, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items in U.S. City Average) is an index with base period 1982-1984 = 100. It is monthly and seasonally adjusted; the not seasonally adjusted version is CPIAUCNS, on the same base. The source is the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).

It is published jointly by the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), from the New Residential Sales release. FRED carries it as Median Sales Price of Houses Sold for the United States (series MSPUS), quarterly, in dollars, not seasonally adjusted. It covers new single-family houses sold, not existing homes.

FRED lists the source of the main effective federal funds rate series (FEDFUNDS, monthly, and DFF, daily) as the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, from its H.15 Selected Interest Rates release. The rate itself is calculated by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, which is the listed source for FRED's separate EFFR series. All are in percent, not seasonally adjusted.
